capability_candidates.name: Identify Contract Type
capability_candidates.description: Classify the contract into one of 15 contract types using key signal phrases.

preconditions.text: Full contract has been read including definitions, schedules, and boilerplate.

structural.text: Output names exactly one Contract Type from the 15-row taxonomy table.

semantic.text: The chosen contract type is consistent with the signal phrases present in the contract.

capability_candidates.name: Plain-Language TL;DR Summary
capability_candidates.description: Produce a 6–10 bullet plain-language summary covering parties, obligations, duration, payment, termination, restrictions, governing law, and top risks.

preconditions.text: All pages have been read without skipping.

structural.text: Summary contains between 6 and 10 bullets.
Bullets cover the 8 required topics (parties, core obligation, duration, payment, termination, restrictions, governing law, special risks).

semantic.text: Each bullet accurately reflects the corresponding clause of the contract in plain language.

capability_candidates.name: Comprehensive Risk Scan (RED/YELLOW/GREEN)
capability_candidates.description: Scan the contract against 15 RED high-risk patterns, 12 YELLOW medium-risk patterns, and standard GREEN items, classifying findings by severity.
outputs: risk findings classified RED/YELLOW/GREEN with clause and recommendation

preconditions.text: Definitions, schedules/annexures, and boilerplate sections have been read since risks often hide there.

structural.text: Findings are categorized into RED, YELLOW, and GREEN sections.
Each RED/YELLOW finding includes Clause, Location, Issue, and Recommendation columns.

semantic.text: Each flagged item matches the definition of its severity tier per the risk patterns table.

common_failure_modes.text: Missing risks that hide in Schedules, Annexures, Exhibits, Appendices.
Missing boilerplate-located risks like jurisdiction, arbitration, liability caps.

capability_candidates.name: Contract-Type-Specific Checks
capability_candidates.description: Run additional checks tailored to the identified contract type (SaaS, Employment, Commercial Lease, Loan/Credit, NDA).

preconditions.text: Contract type has been identified.

structural.text: Checklist items run match the identified contract type's section (e.g. SaaS checks include DPA, data portability, uptime SLA, subprocessors, breach notification).

semantic.text: Each check correctly reports whether the contract addresses the item and whether the term is acceptable.

capability_candidates.name: Renewal & Fee Trap Detection
capability_candidates.description: Identify the 10 renewal and fee trap patterns (auto-renewal, cancellation window, price increases, ETF, minimum commitment, overage, late penalty, etc.) with their impact.

structural.text: Output is a table with columns Trap, Detail/What to Find, and Impact.
Each detected trap maps to one of the 10 listed trap categories.

semantic.text: Reported impact quantifies the trap (e.g., annualized cost, calendar date, ETF amount) where data permits.

capability_candidates.name: Assemble Contract Analysis Report
capability_candidates.description: Compose the final analysis output following the prescribed template: header, TL;DR, Risk Report, Renewal & Fee Traps, type-specific checks, and Risk Score.

preconditions.text: All upstream analyses (summary, risk scan, type-specific checks, renewal traps) have been completed.

structural.text: Report includes header with Contract Type, Parties, and Pages Analyzed.
Report contains sections: TL;DR Summary, Risk Report (RED/YELLOW/GREEN), Renewal & Fee Traps, type-specific checks, Risk Score.
Risk Score table lists counts for RED flags, YELLOW flags, type-specific gaps, and a Recommendation row.

capability_candidates.name: Suggested Clause Rewrites
capability_candidates.description: When asked, provide specific replacement language for RED clauses (e.g. indemnification, auto-renewal, unilateral changes).
matched_terms: specific replacement language for RED clauses

preconditions.text: RED clauses have been identified by the risk scan.

structural.text: Rewrite is provided as a quoted block of replacement contractual language.

semantic.text: Rewrite materially mitigates the identified risk (e.g., caps liability, extends notice, requires mutual consent).

capability_candidates.name: Classify document to processing mode via signal map
capability_candidates.description: Read the first 1-2 pages of an uploaded document and apply the classification signal map to identify the document type and recommended processing mode.

preconditions.text: User has consented to auto-classification before reading the document
Read only the first 1-2 pages (or full document if short)

structural.text: Output states the matched mode name from the signal map
Output includes the signals that led to the classification decision

semantic.text: Classification matches the dominant signals per the signal map (e.g., MRZ → Passport → ID & Passport Scanner)

common_failure_modes.text: Misclassifying a medical document as a form or receipt
Misrouting a document with both form structure and contract clauses (should go to Contract Analyzer)
Misrouting a document with both financial tables and medical results (should go to Medical Summarizer)
Treating a non-document image (selfie, landscape, website screenshot) as a document instead of flagging it

capability_candidates.name: Assess classification confidence and select output flow
capability_candidates.description: Assign a confidence level (High / Medium / Low / Multi-mode) to the classification based on signal strength and choose the corresponding response action (auto-proceed, ask confirmation, present options, or list multiple modes).

preconditions.text: An initial classification has been produced from the signal map

structural.text: High confidence (≥85%) → proceed automatically and state classification at the start
Medium confidence (60–85%) → state classification with brief reasoning and ask for confirmation
Low confidence (<60%) → present top 2-3 options and ask user to choose
Multi-mode → list all applicable modes, recommend one, let user choose

capability_candidates.name: Render classification output in the confidence-appropriate template
capability_candidates.description: Produce the classification output using the prescribed template for High, Medium, Low, or Multi-mode confidence, including document type, mode name, reasoning, and any options offered to the user.

preconditions.text: Classification and confidence have been determined

structural.text: High-confidence output includes 'Document classified as', confidence label, one-line reason, and 'Proceeding with [Mode Name]…'
Medium-confidence output includes document type, mode name, 2-line reason with specific signals, and asks for confirmation with alternative modes
Low-confidence output presents a table of mode options with 'Best For' descriptions
Multi-mode output lists a primary recommendation and also-possible modes with reasons

semantic.text: Stated reason cites the specific signals observed in the document

capability_candidates.name: Load and display timeline
capability_candidates.description: Load the timeline file and display entries as a formatted table with date, mode, document, and summary columns; show an empty-state message when no entries exist.

preconditions.text: Timeline file at ~/.doc-process-timeline.json may or may not exist

structural.text: Output table contains columns: #, Date & Time, Mode, Document, Summary
When no entries exist, display the empty-state message stating '0 documents logged'

capability_candidates.name: Statistics dashboard
capability_candidates.description: Produce a usage statistics dashboard summarizing total documents, most/least used mode, first and most recent entry, and per-mode usage breakdown.

preconditions.text: Timeline file should have 3+ entries

structural.text: Output contains metrics: Total Documents Logged, Most Used Mode, Least Used Mode, First Entry, Most Recent Entry
Output contains Usage by Mode table with Mode, Count, % of Total, Last Used columns

capability_candidates.name: Filtered views
capability_candidates.description: Display the timeline filtered by mode/type, presented in the same table format with a count of matched vs total entries.

preconditions.text: Invoked with --type "<Mode Name>" argument

structural.text: Filtered results presented in same table format as full timeline
Header line states 'Showing [N] of [Total] entries matching: [filter description]'

capability_candidates.name: Save timeline as Markdown report
capability_candidates.description: Export the timeline to a formatted Markdown report at ~/Documents/doc-process-timeline.md containing entries and a usage summary, with no document content included.

preconditions.text: User has confirmed yes to saving prompt

structural.text: Markdown file written to ~/Documents/doc-process-timeline.md
Report contains the N logged entries and a usage summary
Report contains no document content — only type, filename, and one-line summaries
Confirmation message 'Saved to ~/Documents/doc-process-timeline.md — [N] entries.' is emitted

capability_candidates.name: Delete a specific entry
capability_candidates.description: Remove one timeline entry by its id after showing it and obtaining confirmation.

preconditions.text: Entry must be shown to the user and confirmation obtained before deletion
Invoked with --id [entry_id]

structural.text: Targeted entry removed from ~/.doc-process-timeline.json

capability_candidates.name: Clear all entries
capability_candidates.description: Permanently delete all timeline entries from ~/.doc-process-timeline.json after warning the user.

preconditions.text: User has been warned and confirmed

structural.text: All entries removed from ~/.doc-process-timeline.json

capability_candidates.name: Export timeline to JSON
capability_candidates.description: Export the timeline to a JSON file at a specified output path.

structural.text: JSON file written to specified output path (e.g., ~/Documents/timeline.json)

capability_candidates.name: Log entry after consent
capability_candidates.description: Append a new entry to the timeline with type, source, and PII-free one-line summary, only after user has consented; announce 'Logged to your timeline.' after each task.

preconditions.text: User must have explicitly said yes to the consent prompt before any add is executed
If user said no or did not answer, do not run timeline_manager.py add
Summary must not contain names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, account numbers, medical values, or other identifying data

structural.text: New entry written to ~/.doc-process-timeline.json with id, timestamp, type, source, summary fields
After each task, the line 'Logged to your timeline.' is stated
Summary contains only category-level descriptions, no PII

semantic.text: Summary uses category-level descriptions consistent with the Acceptable Summary examples for the given Mode

common_failure_modes.text: Including PII (names, ID numbers, addresses, account numbers, medical values) in the --summary value
Running add without obtaining explicit user consent

capability_candidates.name: Classify Form Type
capability_candidates.description: Classify the uploaded form into a known category (visa, tax, insurance, rental, employment, medical, bank, education, legal, business, event, or generic) based on signal keywords before extracting fields.
matched_terms: Classify the form before extracting fields

preconditions.text: A form document (PDF, image, screenshot, or printed scan) is provided.

structural.text: Output contains a 'Form Type' label.

semantic.text: Assigned form type is consistent with the classification signals present in the document.

common_failure_modes.text: Unknown/ambiguous form forces fall-back to Generic with best-effort matching.

capability_candidates.name: Extract All Form Fields
capability_candidates.description: Read the document visually or structurally and enumerate every fillable field with label, number, type, required/optional flag, format notes, section, and conditional dependencies.
matched_terms: multi-page forms, process page by page and number fields sequentially

preconditions.text: Document is readable visually (image/screenshot) or structurally (PDF text layer).

structural.text: Each extracted field includes label, type, and required/optional status.
Fields are grouped by section as printed on the form.
For multi-page forms, fields are numbered sequentially across pages.

semantic.text: Field labels match exactly as printed on the form.
Conditional fields are flagged with their triggering condition.

capability_candidates.name: Request Required User Data
capability_candidates.description: Present a data-handling notice and then request only the user data needed by the fields actually present on the form, using either single-prompt or field-by-field collection.
matched_terms: Only request fields that actually appear on the form

preconditions.text: Fields have already been extracted so that requests can be scoped to the form's actual fields.

structural.text: Data-handling notice is shown before requesting any personal data.
Prompt only requests fields that actually appear on the form.
Category-specific additions (visa/medical/tax) are included only if such fields exist on the form.

semantic.text: Notice states data is used only in this session, not stored, and that skipped fields will be marked [MISSING].

common_failure_modes.text: Front-loading a large list of sensitive field requests when user chose field-by-field mode.

capability_candidates.name: Match User Data to Form Fields via Aliases
capability_candidates.description: Map user-provided data fields to form labels using the standard and travel/visa alias tables, choosing the most specific match when multiple aliases match.
matched_terms: When multiple aliases match one field, use the most specific match

preconditions.text: User has provided data values for the requested fields.

structural.text: Each filled field corresponds to a data field defined in the alias tables.
When multiple aliases match one field, the most specific match is chosen.

semantic.text: Calculated fields (e.g., Age from DOB, Duration from arrival/departure) are derived correctly.

common_failure_modes.text: Inventing or guessing field values instead of marking them [MISSING].

capability_candidates.name: Validate Filled Values
capability_candidates.description: Apply validation rules on filled values: date format, passport number shape, phone country code, email format, postal code, future-date logic, passport 6-month validity, and DOB/age consistency.

preconditions.text: Fields have been filled with candidate values before validation.

structural.text: Email values contain '@' and a domain.
Passport numbers are non-empty and typically 6–9 alphanumeric characters.
Arrival/departure dates are in the future.
Warning emitted if passport expires within 6 months of travel date.
DOB-derived age matches any explicit Age field.

semantic.text: Date values conform to the form-required format.

capability_candidates.name: Produce Structured Fill Table
capability_candidates.description: Render the filled form as a sectioned markdown table with field number, label, value, type, and status, plus summary counts and dedicated sections for missing fields, action-required items, warnings, and notes.

preconditions.text: Fields have been matched, filled, and validated.

structural.text: Output includes a header line with Total Fields, Filled, Missing, and Action Required counts.
Fields are grouped under Section headings matching the form.
Each row contains #, Field, Value, Type, and Status columns.
Unknown values are rendered as [MISSING — please provide].
Signature and photo fields are flagged as action-required.
Passport/ID numbers are masked (middle digits) when displayed for confirmation.

semantic.text: Output respects form-specified formats such as uppercase, date format, and length limits.

common_failure_modes.text: Including conditional fields when their triggering condition is not met.

capability_candidates.name: Offer Export Options and Supporting-Document Checklist
capability_candidates.description: After presenting the filled table, offer guided completion, JSON export, plain-text export, a form-type-specific supporting-document checklist, and form-specific guidance.
matched_terms: Supporting Document Checklists by Form Type

preconditions.text: Filled table has been presented to the user.

structural.text: JSON export contains all field/value pairs as a JSON object.
Plain-text export uses Key: Value format.
Supporting-document checklist matches the form type's required documents.

semantic.text: Form-specific guidance is relevant to the country/authority (e.g., Schengen ≥ €100/day).

capability_candidates.name: Identity document type detection
capability_candidates.description: Classify the identity document into one of the recognized types (passport, national ID, visa, residence permit, driver's license, birth certificate, voter ID, military ID) using visual signals and MRZ format.

preconditions.text: Input is an image of an identity document showing visual signals or MRZ.

structural.text: Output identifies the document type from the enumerated set in the detection table.
When MRZ is present, the reported MRZ format (TD1/TD2/TD3) matches the table for that document type.

capability_candidates.name: Passport biographic field extraction
capability_candidates.description: Extract the standard ICAO passport biographic fields (surname, given names, nationality, country code, DOB, sex, place of birth, dates, passport number, personal number, issuing authority, endorsements) from a passport biographic page.

preconditions.text: Document is recognized as a passport biographic page.

structural.text: Output includes the passport fields listed in the Passport extraction table (surname, given names, nationality, dates, passport number, etc.).
Nationality is reported as a 3-letter ICAO country code.
Passport number is masked, showing only last 3 characters as XXXXX{last3}.

semantic.text: Extracted values semantically match what is shown on the document image.

common_failure_modes.text: Personal number may be blank (filler `<`) and must not be hallucinated.

capability_candidates.name: Country-specific national ID field extraction
capability_candidates.description: Extract national-ID fields per country convention (EU, India Aadhaar, Singapore NRIC, USA, UK, China, Japan, South Korea, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Brazil).

preconditions.text: Document is recognized as a national ID card for one of the supported countries.

structural.text: Output contains the country-specific field set described for the detected country (e.g., 12-digit Aadhaar for India, S/T/F/G/M prefix + 7 digits + letter for Singapore, 18-digit ID for China).
ID number is masked, showing only last 3 characters as XXXXX{last3}.

capability_candidates.name: Driver's license field extraction
capability_candidates.description: Extract driver's license fields including license number, DOB, address, vehicle classes, restrictions, endorsements, donor status, physical descriptors, and REAL ID / Enhanced ID markers.

preconditions.text: Document is recognized as a driver's license.

structural.text: Output contains the driver's license key fields enumerated in the table (license number, DOB, issue/expiry, address, vehicle classes, restrictions, endorsements, etc.).
License number is masked, showing only last 3 characters as XXXXX{last3}.

capability_candidates.name: MRZ decoding
capability_candidates.description: Decode TD1, TD2, and TD3 MRZ formats into structured fields (document type, country, document number, nationality, DOB, sex, expiry, personal number, name).

preconditions.text: MRZ is present and legible in the document.

structural.text: Decoded fields appear in the positions defined by the selected MRZ format (e.g., TD3 line 2 doc number at positions 1–9, DOB at 14–19, expiry at 22–27).
Dates YYMMDD are expanded to a human-readable date in the decoded output.
Filler `<` characters in fields like personal number are reported as [Not present] rather than raw fillers.

capability_candidates.name: MRZ check digit validation
capability_candidates.description: Compute and verify MRZ check digits using the 7-3-1 weighting algorithm for document number, DOB, expiry, personal number, and composite fields.

preconditions.text: MRZ has been decoded into fields with associated check digit positions.

structural.text: For each MRZ check-digit field (doc number, DOB, expiry, personal number, composite), the report shows raw MRZ, decoded value, check digit, and VALID/INVALID status.
Check digit is computed by assigning char values (0-9 face value, A-Z = 10-35, `<` = 0), applying weights 7,3,1 repeating, summing products, and taking modulo 10.
Composite check digit covers doc number + DOB + expiry + personal number.

capability_candidates.name: Document validity assessment
capability_candidates.description: Assess document validity: expiry status, six-month travel rule, MRZ integrity, document type recognition, and legibility.

preconditions.text: Document fields including expiry date have been extracted and MRZ check digits computed.

structural.text: Output includes the six validity rows: expired?, valid-for-travel 6-month rule, MRZ integrity, document type recognized, legibility, possible issues.
Expiry status is computed against the extracted Date of Expiry and reports remaining time.
MRZ integrity row reports pass/fail across all check digits.

capability_candidates.name: Identity data privacy redaction
capability_candidates.description: Apply privacy rules: mask document/ID/personal numbers to last 3 characters and append the required disclaimer; never store or transmit extracted data.

preconditions.text: Identity fields have been extracted prior to output formatting.

structural.text: All document numbers, ID numbers, and personal numbers in output are masked as XXXXX{last3}, showing only last 3 characters.
Output includes the required disclaimer text about personal-reference-only use and lack of authenticity verification.

common_failure_modes.text: Echoing full document/ID/personal numbers instead of masking violates privacy rules.
Logging, storing, or transmitting extracted identity data violates privacy rules.
